messages:
mike: Quick proposal idea — ingress should do a 2-phase session-cutover for long-lived streaming requests so midflight handoffs are consistent and idempotent. Sketch below.
anna: high-level please — what problem does this solve vs current resume-token approach?
mike: current resume-token works for retransmit but not for consumer-side cutover when we move a session between edge pods. We see duped partial outputs or orphaned leases. 2-phase: PREPARE (drain + snapshot token), COMMIT (atomic handoff) with explicit lease ID and commit ack. If COMMIT fails, receiver retries PREPARE using same lease id and aborts previous.
ravi: sounds similar to DB two-phase commit but for the streaming session. How do we avoid adding a blocking barrier that hurts latency for short-lived requests?
mike: good call. We make it optional and only trigger for sessions that exceed a threshold (e.g., 30s or >N tokens) or when control-plane signals a migration. For <threshold we keep best-effort resume token only.
sarah: how does this interact with hedging & region fallback? If a hedged request races, we must ensure only one COMMIT succeeds or outputs are deduplicated upstream.
mike: plan: session metadata includes a monotonic commit epoch + lease id. Edge offers lease to candidate pod. The commit path checks epoch/lease to accept only the highest-epoch commit. Hedged replicas attach their chosen lease; the first COMMIT wins and others abort. Upstream clients dedupe using final session id and per-chunk sequence numbers.
anna: can we implement this without changing client SDKs? We can't force customers to change headers mid-rollout.
mike: we wrap it in gateway behavior. SDKs see same stream semantics. Internally we attach opaque headers (x-rw-session, x-rw-lease) and change nothing in the user-level protocol. Only customers parsing internals would notice.
jordan: what's failure mode if we lose commit ack? e.g., COMMIT accepted but ack from target fails to get back to origin.
mike: origin retries ack path with exponential backoff. If persistent unknown, a background reconciler claims the lease expired after TTL and either acts as arbitrator or forces abort. We plan to emit metrics for "commit-ack-latency" and "commit-ack-timeout" to catch flakes.
sarah: we should avoid cross-node synchronized clocks for TTL. Use lease heartbeat from accepting pod instead.
ravi: what about memory / kv cache for partial KV caches (kv-cache of attn keys) — we can't copy large KV caches across pods.
mike: yes — we don't move KV caches. Instead the PREPARE will include a small manifest: prefix length, last-token-index, and an object pointing to a shared checkpoint blob (S3-like or local blobstore). The target pod will fetch KV state on-demand using the checkpoint as async cold-start while serving resumed stream with tokens reconstructed from prefix cache + remote fetch. This trades cold-start IO for correctness.
anna: rollout strategy?
mike: phased: opt-in flag on routes -> enable in canary cluster -> enable for long-lived sessions only -> expose debug metrics -> default off for 2 weeks -> enable org-wide. CLI toggle for support to disable per-customer.
sarah: add test matrix: simulate hedged races + commit ack lost + blobstore latency. Also load test for 99th pct tail when PREPARE happens.
jordan: +1 on tests. Also add tracing tags: session.lease, session.epoch, session.source-pod, session-target-pod.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: ingress/session-cutover-v1 -> canary cluster
anna: ok thanks. Action items: mike write RFC with state diagram + sequence diagram, ravi to list performance guardrails, sarah to draft tests, jordan to add tracing proposal. I'll schedule a 30min follow-up next Tue. :thumbsup:
